title: The Marseille assassination, 1934 — the king who feared Tuesdays
sources: Wikipedia: Alexander I of Yugoslavia — after the deaths of three family members on Tuesdays, Alexander refused public functions on that day of the week; on Tuesday 9 October 1934 he had no choice, arriving in Marseille for a state visit to France; driven slowly through the streets with French foreign minister Louis Barthou; Vlado Chernozemski, a member of the pro-Bulgarian Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organization (IMRO), which worked with the Croat Ustaše of Ante Pavelić, stepped into the street and shot the king and the chauffeur; Alexander died in the car; it was one of the first assassinations captured on film — the newsreel cameraman was only metres away; the exact moment was not filmed, the events before and the aftermath were; Barthou was killed by a stray bullet fired by French police — a 1935 ballistic report, kept from the public until 1974, showed he was hit by a round of the type carried by French police; about 500,000 people attended his funeral in Belgrade

Wikipedia: Vlado Chernozemski — born Velichko Kerin in Kamenitsa (now Velingrad), Bulgaria; IMRO member; trained a group of Ustaše in camps in Italy and Hungary; on 9 October the motorcade drove at 8 km/h; he leapt onto the car's running board; died after the attack
Wikipedia: Louis Barthou — French foreign minister; a bullet struck his arm and severed an artery; the ballistic report showed a French police revolver round

Also on this day (candidates.md / Wikipedia On This Day): 1676 Antonie van Leeuwenhoek wrote to the Royal Society describing 'animalcules'; 1888 the Washington Monument opened, then the world's tallest building; 1604 Kepler's Supernova, the most recent observed in the Milky Way

Archive film (public domain): Universal Newsreel '1934-10-17 King Alexander Assassination' — the arrival on the destroyer Dubrovnik, the king and Barthou in the car, the crowd; the scenes of the dead king are not used

Photos (public domain): King Alexander portrait; Louis Barthou (Bain); L'Illustration album 'La tragédie du 9 octobre'; Mundo Gráfico, 17 October 1934; the funeral in Belgrade; Marseille, La Canebière (1930s postcard); TIME cover, 1929

post.facebook:
On this day in 1934, King Alexander I of Yugoslavia was assassinated in Marseille.

Alexander had lost three relatives on Tuesdays, and avoided public duties on that day of the week. But his state visit to France began on Tuesday, 9 October 1934.

As he rode slowly through the streets beside French foreign minister Louis Barthou, a newsreel cameraman was filming just metres away. A gunman leapt onto the car and shot the king and his driver. He was Vlado Chernozemski, a Bulgarian revolutionary of the IMRO, working with the Croat Ustaše. The king died in the car — one of the first assassinations caught on film.

Barthou was hit in the arm and bled to death. A ballistic report, kept from the public until 1974, showed the bullet that killed him came from a French police gun.

Also on 9 October: Leeuwenhoek first described microscopic "animalcules" (1676), and the Washington Monument opened (1888).

youtube.description:
King Alexander I of Yugoslavia had lost three relatives on Tuesdays, and avoided public duties on that day. On Tuesday 9 October 1934, his state visit to France began in Marseille — and a newsreel camera was rolling metres away when a gunman leapt onto his car. The king was killed; so was France's foreign minister Louis Barthou. A ballistic report hidden until 1974 showed Barthou's fatal bullet came from a French police gun.

Also on 9 October: Leeuwenhoek's 'animalcules' (1676), the Washington Monument opens (1888).
